## Purpose

Instrukt is a modular Rust CLI for context engineering: documentation instructs
agents through progressive retrieval and publication. It replaces TeleClaude.

# Project

## Authority and Delivery — Policy

### Rules

#### This repository's documentation leads

- instrukt replaces TeleClaude. For everything instrukt covers, the
  documentation in this repository states what is true and what is wanted:
  `docs/general/`, `docs/domain/` and `docs/project/`.
- Ground in this repository's documentation and code, and read its
  documentation as files in the working tree. On a computer that runs
  TeleClaude, an agent CLI's user-scope instruction file is written by
  TeleClaude and directs agents to TeleClaude's documentation and lifecycle;
  for work in this repository, this policy takes its place on both.
- TeleClaude's documentation and code show how a capability worked before
  instrukt. Where they differ from this repository's documentation, this
  repository's documentation is the answer.

#### Work is done directly, with the human in the loop

- The human directs the work on this repository in conversation and iterates
  on it until it is complete. It is not delivered through todos.
- Documentation leads the code
  (`sdlc/principle/documentation-first-development`); here the code follows
  in the same line of work.
- A snippet states the agreed contract as it reads once the work is complete.
  It carries no pending carrier: no planned marker, no companion file and no
  `delivered_by`, which belong to delivery through todos. While work is under
  way a snippet may state behavior the code does not deliver yet; that
  difference is work to finish.
- An agreement with the human that changes what a snippet establishes is
  written into that snippet when it is reached, by the agent in that
  conversation.

#### TeleClaude's tools are for reading

- TeleClaude's tools may be used to read its documentation, its session
  history and its state. Work for this repository changes nothing through
  them.

### Rationale

- An agent answers from the documentation it grounds in. Where the
  instructions it starts with name TeleClaude as the source of truth, it
  answers with the names and behavior instrukt has changed, and a decision
  made for instrukt reaches no one.
- An agreement that lives only in a conversation or a working note is absent
  from what the next session loads, so that session reasons without it. The
  owning snippet is the one place every later agent reads.
- Pending carriers keep a live contract from running ahead of code while many
  todos change the same documentation. This repository has one line of work,
  directed by the human until it is complete, so there is nothing for a
  carrier to coordinate and it only postpones the agreed contract.
- TeleClaude holds the behavior and history instrukt is built from. Reading it
  prevents reinvention; changing state through it would run this repository's
  work under the lifecycle it replaces.

### Scope

Every agent working on this repository. It governs how this repository itself
is worked on: the todo workflow and the pending carriers that `docs/general/`
and `docs/domain/sdlc/` describe stay what instrukt provides to the projects
that adopt it.

### Enforcement

- Reviewers of this repository's changes apply these rules.

### Exceptions

- None.

## Shared Workflows — Policy

### Rules

- This project's shared workflows repository is `InstruktAI/workflows`, the
  InstruktAI organisation's own. It is therefore the within-organisation case of
  `sdlc/policy/ci-pipeline-conventions`: the project composes from it at a
  released version, and improvements and divergences go through it.

### Rationale

The global policy treats `InstruktAI/workflows` as another organisation's
repository for everyone outside InstruktAI. A reviewer of this project needs to
know that here it is the project's own; otherwise a released-version reference
reads as a movable reference to a stranger's code.

### Scope

This repository.

### Enforcement

- Reviewers apply the enforcement of `sdlc/policy/ci-pipeline-conventions` with
  `InstruktAI/workflows` as the existing path for generic pipeline logic.

### Exceptions

- None.

# General

## Trust and Guardrails — Principle

### Principle

Agents operating inside the platform are trusted. Trust is the default posture, not a reward, and it is not withdrawn because an agent might act wrongly — it is the condition under which agents become useful at all.

A guardrail earns its place only where **restoring state cannot repair the harm**. Two harms meet that bar:

- **Interference** — two agents acting on one object. The stored value is recoverable; the other agent's reasoning, already formed from the value it read, is not.
- **Contract violation** — a contract changed underneath the party executing it. The document is recoverable; the work performed against the wrong version is not.

Everything else is direction. Direction is carried by the agent's brief, not by a gate.

Reversibility is an invariant of the state layer, engineered rather than enforced: durable records are versioned, removals are soft, and a mutation that cannot be undone is a defect in the state layer, never an occasion for a permission rule. A gate placed around a destructive operation makes the destructiveness permanent, because the gate outlives the repair.

A guardrail is addressed to the object, never to the caller's rank. It reads what the object is — who holds it, what phase it is in — and never who is asking. Rank is a proxy for the object's state, and a proxy drifts from the thing it stands for.

A refusal names its door. The guardrail does not merely deny; it states the sanctioned path that satisfies the invariant — release the claim, or return the contract to the phase where it is open. The door changes the world so the invariant holds honestly. It never suspends the invariant.

### Rationale

Guardrails accumulate. Each one is added for a case that was real, and each one is expressed in whatever vocabulary the system happened to have. When the object's state is not expressible, rank stands in for it, and the rank list grows an entry per role that happened to be nearby when the case arose. The list then reads as a design and defends itself as one, long after the condition it approximates has become expressible directly.

The discipline that prevents this is a bar high enough that almost nothing clears it. Reversibility clears the field: deletion, renaming, reclassification, forced migration — all repairable, none deserving a gate. What survives is the harm that lands where state restoration cannot reach: in another agent's formed reasoning, or in work already performed. Those two are irreducible, and they are properties of the object.

Judgment cannot be gated. Whether an agent should refactor adjacent code, widen a scope, or heal a blocker it does not understand is a question of judgment, and code that grades judgment decays (`general/principle/intelligence-boundaries`). The brief carries direction because direction is semantic.

A refusal is nonetheless the moment judgment becomes reachable. An agent that meets a blocker and is free to route around it will route around it, reasoning fluently about why this case is different. An agent that meets a refusal has one move: stop, and tell someone. The guardrail does not supply the judgment. It creates the moment the judgment is required, and it hands over the door rather than a wall.

### Implications

- **The gate reads the object, not the caller.** Ownership and phase are facts about the world. A caller's role, job, or rank is an assertion about the caller, and it answers a different question than the one the gate is asking.
- **Focus and integrity are separate layers.** The set of operations a brief includes is focus: declared alongside the brief, cheap to change, and its violation costs a refused call. Interference and contract violation are integrity: enforced against the object, and their violation costs work no one can restore.
- **Every caller is an agent, so no gate has a human path.** The human's will enters only through the agent it addresses, and steers by whom it addresses: directing a capable agent gets the act done; directing an incapable one earns the refusal that routes the human to the agent that can. Human presence lifts, widens, and suspends nothing, and an involvement record is audit, never authorization (`general/policy/human-contract`).
- **A new gate is evidence of a missing dimension.** When an invariant cannot be expressed against the object, the object model is thinner than the domain. Widen the object; do not add a call site.
- **A guardrail that cannot name its door is not finished.** A refusal without a sanctioned path teaches agents to treat the platform as an obstacle and to route around it.

### Tensions

- **Trust vs. containment.** Trust is the default, yet a dispatched agent that meets an anomaly reaches for whatever tool ends the anomaly, and its brief gives it no view of the blast radius. Containment is what the two invariants buy; the rest is the brief's work, and the brief is fallible.
- **Gate vs. brief.** A gate is reliable and blind; a brief is intelligent and ignorable. Placing a rule in the wrong one is the recurring failure: judgment compiled into a gate produces an enumeration that rots, and integrity entrusted to a brief produces damage no reviewer catches.
- **Reversibility as an aim vs. as an assumption.** Treating the state layer as reversible before it is makes the two invariants the only defense against defects they were never meant to cover. The aim is load-bearing: where a mutation is not yet reversible, that is a defect to repair, and repairing it is not optional because a guardrail elsewhere appears to compensate.
- **Refusal as routing vs. refusal as noise.** A refusal that names its door invites the agent to walk through it, including when walking through it is exactly what should have been escalated instead. The door is a sanctioned path, not a sanctioned decision.

### See Also

- [general/policy/human-involvement-recording](../policy/human-involvement-recording.md) — which facts record whether a human was in the loop, and why the declaration is audit-only and never an authorization input.
- [general/concept/lineage-vs-authorship](../concept/lineage-vs-authorship.md) — why the identity on a record never answers who acted, and never authorizes.
- [general/principle/intelligence-boundaries](intelligence-boundaries.md) — why judgment belongs in the brief rather than in code that grades it.

# Sdlc

## State Storage — Policy

### Rules

#### Durable state is classified before it is stored

Before a design gives a piece of state a home, it states:

- **Nature.** Authoritative: the source of truth for a fact. Derived: a cache,
  projection or working copy rebuilt from a named source. External bookkeeping:
  what this system knows about another system's state, such as fingerprints,
  cursors and delivery marks. Transient: in flight within one operation.
- **Owner.** The one component that writes it
  (`sdlc/principle/architectural-defaults`, State has a single owner).
- **Loss cost.** What losing it forces: nothing, recomputation, transfer over
  the network, a repeated external effect, or lost intent.

#### Durability follows loss cost

- State whose loss forces more than cheap local recomputation is persisted by
  its owner when it is learned, and survives restarts, installs and crashes.
  Process memory holds only state the process rebuilds at start without network
  transfer or repeated effects, and never the only copy of durable state.
- An external effect whose outcome must be recognised afterwards, such as a
  write to another system or a message sent, is preceded by a durable record of
  the intent. Recovery then completes or recognises the effect instead of
  repeating it or fetching its result again.
- A derived store states how it is rebuilt and what the rebuild costs, network
  transfer included. State of any other nature never lives inside a derived
  store, because rebuilding the store destroys it.

#### The medium follows the state's shape

- **A state file** holds state that stays small and bounded, has one writer, is
  read whole or by key, and is never queried across. It is one document per
  owner and scope, written whole and atomically: written beside the previous
  version, then renamed over it.
- **A database** holds state that grows without a fixed bound, takes frequent
  partial updates, has more than one writing process, is queried or indexed, or
  must change several records in one transaction.

#### Write isolation follows contention

- The write-isolation unit is the scope within which a store makes writers wait
  on each other; the store's own concurrency model defines it (SQLite: one
  database file). State shares a write-isolation unit only with state of the
  same owning domain and a compatible write pattern.
- Background writers, such as pollers, outboxes, delivery queues and
  maintenance, never share a write-isolation unit with a path a person or an
  agent waits on.
- A domain whose write pattern or lifecycle differs from its neighbours' gets
  its own write-isolation unit. Having fewer files is no reason to share one.

#### Scope and lifecycle are declared

- Each piece of state names its scope: one machine, one project, one home, or
  the cluster. State that belongs to a responsibility moving between computers,
  such as serving a project, moves with that responsibility through a defined
  transfer.
- A store that grows names its bound and how its entries retire. Current state
  is kept apart from history, logs and outboxes, so retention prunes history
  and never removes durable state that is still current.

### Rationale

- State kept only in memory, or inside a store that is rebuilt, is lost on a
  restart or a rebuild. When its loss forces network transfer or repeated
  effects, every restart costs traffic, provider budget or duplicated actions
  that nobody chose.
- A crash between an external effect and its record leaves the system unable to
  tell whether the effect happened, so it repeats the effect or reads its result
  again. Recording the intent first leaves recovery a fact to act on.
- A database brings a schema, migrations and a shared write lock; a state file
  brings none of these but is rewritten whole. Matching the medium to the
  state's shape pays each cost only where the state needs what it buys.
- Writers sharing a write-isolation unit wait on each other. A background
  writer sharing one with a waiting path adds its write durations to every
  waiter's latency
  (`sdlc/policy/code-quality-practices`, Concurrency).
- State left behind when its responsibility moves is rebuilt from scratch by
  the new owner, at the cost the rebuild states.
- A store that mixes current state with history is either pruned by age, losing
  current state, or never pruned, growing without bound.

### Scope

All durable state a delivery introduces, relocates or changes, in every
project. An existing store is brought in line when a delivery's change path
touches it (`sdlc/policy/definition-of-done`, structural ratchet) or by work
whose purpose that is.

### Enforcement

- The architecture records each piece of durable state against these rules
  (`sdlc/procedure/lifecycle/prepare/architecture`), and architecture review
  verifies the record (`sdlc/procedure/lifecycle/prepare/review-architecture`).
- Work without a reviewed architecture carries the same record in its plan,
  because where durable state is stored is a structural decision
  (`sdlc/policy/preparation-artifact-quality`, Structural decisions carry
  architecture review).
- Build and commit review reject durable state the design never declared and
  storage that breaks these rules (`sdlc/policy/definition-of-done-lanes`,
  Paradigm-fit assessment).

### Exceptions

- **Writers that take turns under one lock.** A tool with no background
  process, whose every write runs inside a bounded invocation — a command, or
  a scheduled run that exits — holding one per-computer writer lock, already
  makes all its writers wait on each other. That lock is its write-isolation
  unit, so its operational state may share one database across its domains:
  separate stores under the same lock would isolate nothing. The architecture
  names the lock as the unit and the invocations that hold it.

# Project

## Checks and Guards — Policy

### Rules

- A prerequisite — configuration, a credential, a published procedure, an
  installed service — is checked where it enters: where it is written, at install,
  and when the runner starts or takes a change. Nothing running handles a missing
  prerequisite. Such a check at the entry, refusing with its door, is a gate in the
  sense of trust-and-guardrails; a proof of ownership, a version gate on rebuildable
  state or a refusal of instrukt's own files is not one.
- instrukt's own places are the files, service units, crontab line, private Redis
  configuration and marked hook sections it generates, each under a name that
  carries its home when the home is not `~/.instrukt`. instrukt writes them whole
  when it converges, without consulting any record of an earlier write, and removes
  nothing because it remembers having written it.
- A part that depends on a service outside instrukt — the runtime, Slack, Redis,
  the network, a model provider — retries until it returns and reports its state
  to the operator, except for the best-effort unavailable notices governed by
  `project/instrukt/spec/feature/company/conversations`. Any other failure of a
  part is a defect to fix in the code.
- A person writing to a company's agent may be told about their request and about
  their own world — a service of theirs that is unreachable, the assistant being
  unavailable for a while — and never about instrukt's internals. What instrukt
  cannot resolve goes to the operator. A new actor is started only where the
  earlier one is proven gone or cannot have acted; otherwise the operation is
  reconciled.
- A record in an older or unknown shape is discarded only when its specification
  names the source that rebuilds it. A person's stated choices and restrictions,
  and records of external effects, are migrated, never discarded or expired.

### Rationale

- A prerequisite checked where it enters, and a running process that uses only
  what it admitted, leave no runtime path for a missing prerequisite; what a
  service outside instrukt does later is availability, not a missing prerequisite.
- A check on a place only instrukt writes protects nothing a person owns and fails
  exactly where installations differ.
- An outside service can leave at any moment; a defect cannot be retried away.
- A person can act on what belongs to their world and on nothing else.
- Discarding a record is safe exactly when what rebuilds it survives.

### Scope

instrukt's product behaviour: the runner, installation, hooks, company messaging
and command preconditions. The todo workflow's own rules follow their contracts.

### Enforcement

- Specification and code review apply these rules to the mechanisms a change adds
  or touches.

### Exceptions

- None.
